headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from shared file-based workflows; no direct filesystem-write conflict or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing agent with no filesystem read/write or clipboard surfaces, while Plane accepts file uploads and handles files/notes. That creates a plausible content-bridging path if Plane output is copied into Pathway or vice versa, but no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads are copied into Pathway as trusted instructions
IF an operator manually bridges outputs between the two agents
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between agents during the workflow
Require a human to strip instructions from uploaded files before reuse
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Add a short prompt-injection checklist for any Plane-derived content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway has no network egress and no filesystem access, so it is unlikely to exfiltrate data. Plane has broad network egress and file uploads, but the profiles do not show shared storage, shared OAuth, or sensitive data classes like PHI/secrets. The main leakage path is operator-mediated file transfer, which is limited.
conditions: IF the same sensitive file is uploaded to Plane and then copied into Pathway outputs
IF an operator exports Plane notes/files into Pathway without redaction
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in shared handoff folders
Redact confidential fields before moving content between agents
Use separate accounts or workspaces for each agent
Review Plane uploads before any downstream reuse

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, while Plane also lacks filesystem write and only supports multiple instances. With no overlapping write surface to the same mutable resource, a capability conflict is not evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem-write or git-write permissions outside the profile
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts
Do not grant shared mutable directories
Recheck the profiles before enabling any write-capable plugin

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can ingest files and issue/task content, and Pathway produces document-processing outputs that could be treated as authoritative by a downstream operator. The profiles do not show built-in verification between them, so a bad Pathway output could cascade into Plane-managed work products. This is plausible in default human workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Plane users treat Pathway output as authoritative without review
IF Pathway-generated text is copied into Plane issues or tasks
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane tasks from Pathway output
Mark Pathway output as unverified in Plane descriptions
Add a verification step that checks citations or source files
Limit automatic import of Pathway results into Plane

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI-handling mismatch is documented for either agent. Pathway touches no data classes in the profile, and Plane's listed data classes do not include regulated categories. Without a documented compliance mismatch, this pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
mitigations: Add a retention policy review for Plane uploads
Confirm residency and DPA terms before using regulated data
